issues.t: IMS bearing failure
issues.sym: Often no warning at all. Some cars show metal flakes in the oil filter, an oil drip from the back of the engine, or a rattle or knock from the rear of the engine before it seizes.
issues.why: The intermediate shaft (IMS) bearing on the regular Carrera engines is a sealed bearing that can lose its grease and wear out. When it fails, the cam timing is lost and debris goes through the engine. Single-row bearings fitted around 2002-2005 carry the highest risk. Turbo, GT2 and GT3 engines use a different design and are not affected.
issues.next: Ask for records showing the bearing was upgraded. If not, many owners have an upgraded bearing fitted when the clutch is next replaced. Have the oil filter cut open and checked for metal at each service. If you hear a new knock, stop driving.

issues.t: Cylinder bore scoring and oil burning
issues.sym: Blue smoke, especially at start-up, rising oil use, a sooty tailpipe on one bank only, a ticking or tapping noise at idle, and sometimes misfire codes from oily spark plugs.
issues.why: The cylinder walls in the 3.6 and 3.8 engines can get scratched (scored) by the pistons. Once scored, oil gets past the rings and is burned.
issues.next: Have a specialist do a borescope (camera) inspection of the cylinders before buying or as soon as oil use goes up. A badly scored engine needs a rebuild with new cylinder liners, so get a firm diagnosis before spending money elsewhere.

issues.t: Air-oil separator failure (smoke on start-up)
issues.sym: Big clouds of white or blue smoke right after starting, oil smell, rough idle, high oil use, or a check engine light for lean running. The oil filler may be hard to remove because of strong suction.
issues.why: The air-oil separator vents crankcase gases and returns oil to the sump. When its inner diaphragm tears or its hoses crack, oil is pulled into the intake and burned. Overfilling the oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level on level ground and do not overfill. If smoke and oil use continue, have the separator and its vent hoses checked; it is a fairly affordable part. Do not keep driving with heavy smoke, because a large gulp of oil can damage the engine.

issues.t: Rear main seal oil leak
issues.sym: Oil drips or a damp area where the engine meets the gearbox, under the middle-rear of the car.
issues.why: The seal at the back of the crankshaft can leak, often because the crankcase seal bore was machined slightly off-center at the factory. Replacing the seal alone does not always stop the leak.
issues.next: A small seep is not urgent but should be watched. The gearbox has to come out to replace it, so most owners do it together with a clutch or IMS bearing job.

issues.t: Water pump failure and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant drips or pink/crusty residue near the pump, a coolant smell, the temperature gauge rising, or a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: The water pump has a plastic impeller and a seal that wear out. The impeller can crack and send bits into the cooling system, which can cause hot spots and even cracked cylinder heads.
issues.next: If the temperature climbs, pull over and turn the engine off. Many specialists replace the pump about every 60,000 miles as prevention, along with the thermostat.

issues.t: Cracked coolant expansion tank
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, drips or residue under the engine lid, or a low-coolant warning light.
issues.why: The plastic coolant expansion tank ages, and its seams or bleed valve crack and leak, so the system loses pressure.
issues.next: Top up with the correct Porsche coolant and have the tank pressure-tested. Replace it before it leads to overheating.

issues.t: Cracked cylinder head or oil and coolant mixing
issues.sym: Milky oil, oil in the coolant tank, white exhaust smoke, overheating, or coolant loss with no outside leak.
issues.why: A cylinder head can crack from a hot spot, often after a water pump fails or debris blocks coolant passages. A failed oil cooler or a leaking seal can also mix oil and coolant.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the oil and coolant checked. A specialist can rule out the cheaper cause (the oil cooler) before the engine is opened up.

issues.t: Coolant pipes separating on Turbo models
issues.sym: Sudden coolant loss, a puddle under the engine, steam, or overheating.
issues.why: On the 996 Turbo engine, the coolant pipes are glued into the engine fittings. The glue can let go and a pipe can push out.
issues.next: If you see a large coolant leak, do not drive. The lasting fix is pinning or welding the pipes, which is an engine-out job, so ask whether it has already been done.

issues.t: Clogged or corroded front radiators and A/C condensers
issues.sym: Engine running warmer than normal, weak air conditioning, coolant leaks at the front of the car, or leaves visible in the front bumper intakes.
issues.why: The radiators and A/C condensers sit behind the front bumper openings. Leaves and dirt collect there, hold moisture and corrode the cores.
issues.next: Have the bumper intakes cleaned out regularly. If a radiator or condenser is leaking, replace it before the engine overheats or the A/C gas escapes.

issues.t: Misfire from cracked ignition coils
issues.sym: Flashing or steady check engine light, rough running, shaking at idle, or loss of power.
issues.why: The ignition coils sit on top of the spark plugs and crack from engine heat and water splash.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Coils are often replaced as a set with the spark plugs; PistonHeads says they typically need replacing every 50,000 miles.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner and guide wear
issues.sym: A rattle at cold start that fades, or a cam-timing check engine light.
issues.why: Tensioners weaken and the plastic tensioner pads can break, and chains stretch, especially with long oil-change intervals.
issues.next: Have the cam timing (deviation) values checked with a scan tool. Replace worn tensioners before a chain can jump a tooth.

issues.t: Dropped intake valve seat
issues.sym: Sudden loud ticking or knocking, misfire on one cylinder, and loss of power.
issues.why: On the later 3.6 and 3.8 engines, an intake valve seat can come loose in the cylinder head. Broken pieces can damage the valve, piston and head.
issues.next: Stop the engine right away if a new knock appears. A specialist will need to inspect the cylinder head.

issues.t: Front suspension creaks and worn bushings
issues.sym: Creaking or clunking from the front over bumps, vague steering, or tires wearing on the inside edge.
issues.why: Rubber bushings in the front control arms and the springs and shocks wear with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and the alignment checked. Replacing worn parts together saves labor.

issues.t: Manual gear shift cable breakage
issues.sym: The gear lever goes loose or will not select some gears.
issues.why: The cables connecting the manual gear lever to the gearbox can break.
issues.next: Have the shift cables inspected. A car with a broken cable may be stuck in one gear, so arrange a tow if needed.

issues.t: Blue smoke and oil burning from worn valve guides
issues.sym: Blue smoke at cold start and the engine using more oil than normal.
issues.why: On the air-cooled 993 engine, the valve guides wear from heat and the piston rings can wear too, letting oil into the cylinders.
issues.next: Track how much oil you add. Light smoke for a moment at start-up is common; heavy smoke or much higher use means a specialist should do a leak-down test.

issues.t: Clogged secondary air injection (check engine light)
issues.sym: Check engine light, often with secondary air system codes, and a failed emissions inspection.
issues.why: US 993s have a secondary air system that blows air into the exhaust ports. Carbon builds up in those small passages and blocks them.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the air passages in the cylinder heads usually fixes it, but it is a long job.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers and oil lines
issues.sym: Oil drips under the car, burning oil smell, and in bad cases a drop in oil pressure.
issues.why: Valve covers can warp from heat, and the main seals and oil line fittings age. A failed oil line fitting can dump a lot of oil.
issues.next: Have the source found. If the oil pressure drops, stop the engine at once to avoid serious damage.

issues.t: Clutch master or slave cylinder leak
issues.sym: A soft or sinking clutch pedal, trouble getting into gear, or fluid near the pedal or gearbox.
issues.why: The hydraulic seals in the clutch master and slave cylinders wear and leak.
issues.next: Check the brake/clutch fluid level and have the leak found. Replace the leaking cylinder and bleed the system.

issues.t: GT3 engine connecting rod failure (recall)
issues.sym: Engine damage, oil leaks, or smoke and fire risk on early 2014 GT3s.
issues.why: On GT3s built from October 2013 to January 2014, a connecting rod connection could come loose and break the crankcase. Leaking oil could reach hot parts and start a fire.
issues.next: Porsche told owners not to drive until the engine was replaced. Check that the recall engine replacement has been done.

issues.t: Front hood may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The front lid may not stay securely closed and could open while driving.
issues.why: Front hood lock parts built out of specification may not latch properly.
issues.next: Have a Porsche dealer replace the front hood lock for free.

issues.t: Water in the front footwell from loose A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the front footwell, a damp smell, or electrical faults after rain or A/C use.
issues.why: The A/C drain pipes on early 991s can come loose, so water drains into the cabin instead of out under the car. Left alone it can reach electronics under the floor.
issues.next: Dry the carpet and have the drain pipes refitted soon to protect the electronics.

issues.t: Engine misfire from coil pack or crank sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light, shaking or rough running, and loss of power.
issues.why: Each cylinder has its own coil pack, and a failing coil makes that cylinder misfire. A failing crankshaft sensor can cause similar symptoms. Some 991.2 owners also saw occasional misfires that cleared on their own.
issues.next: Have the codes read to find which cylinder or sensor is at fault.

issues.t: PDK gearbox warnings or skipped gears
issues.sym: A transmission fault message, harsh or jerky shifts, or the gearbox skipping even-numbered gears.
issues.why: The PDK dual-clutch gearbox on the 991 can throw faults that are usually software related. Clutch and fluid wear also matter.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Many cases are fixed with a software update. Keep up with PDK fluid and filter changes.

issues.t: Water pump leak on 3.0L turbo
issues.sym: Coolant drops or crust near the pump, a low coolant warning, or a sweet smell.
issues.why: Water pumps on the 3.0 turbo engine leaked, mostly on cars built from late 2017 to early 2018. Porsche replaced some with sturdier units.
issues.next: Check whether the pump was replaced under warranty. If coolant is dropping, have it pressure-tested.

issues.t: Airbag control unit capacitor fault (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the airbag control unit's power supply can fail, so the airbags may switch off or go off when they shouldn't.
issues.next: Have a dealer update the software and replace the airbag control unit if needed. It's free.

issues.t: Seat side airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign.
issues.why: The initiator in the seat-mounted side airbag may not fire in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the side airbag modules for free.

issues.t: Cabriolet and Targa windshield not properly bonded (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign, though a poorly bonded windshield can sometimes let in wind noise or water.
issues.why: On some 2017 Cabriolets and Targas, the windshield was not bonded correctly and could come loose in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer re-bond the windshield for free.

issues.t: Windshield and rear window may detach (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign until a crash.
issues.why: The front windshield and rear window may not be secured properly. In a crash they could detach and stop the front airbags working as designed.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and replace the glass as needed. It's free.

issues.t: Dashboard can break during passenger airbag deployment (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The dashboard console can break when the passenger airbag goes off, so the airbag may not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the dashboard for free.

issues.t: Center-lock wheel bolt may fracture (recall)
issues.sym: A wheel that feels loose, vibrates or clunks. Porsche told owners not to drive until repaired.
issues.why: The center-lock wheel bolt on some cars may crack, and the wheel could come off.
issues.next: Don't drive the car until a dealer has checked and replaced faulty parts. It's free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not show (recall)
issues.sym: The screen shows no camera picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A driver-assistance software fault can stop the reverse camera image from showing.
issues.next: Have a dealer update the software for free. Until then, check around the car before reversing.

issues.t: Low beams can glare at oncoming drivers (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash their lights at you even on low beam.
issues.why: A software error in the front lighting control module can aim the low beams too high.
issues.next: Have a dealer update the lighting module software for free.

issues.t: 12-volt battery going flat when parked
issues.sym: The car won't start or shows battery warnings after sitting for a few weeks.
issues.why: The 992 draws power while parked, and owners report flat batteries as one of the most common issues. Some report trickle chargers switching off after several weeks.
issues.next: If the car sits, use a battery maintainer that Porsche approves and check it is still charging. Have the battery tested if it keeps going flat.

issues.t: Reduced power and misfire feel from active engine mount fault
issues.sym: A 'reduced engine power' warning, shuddering under gentle acceleration, or a feeling like one cylinder isn't firing.
issues.why: Seals on the active drivetrain mounts can leak and let water reach the electronics, which can trigger these symptoms.
issues.next: Have the fault codes read and the engine mounts checked by a dealer, especially if the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Interior rattles and squeaks
issues.sym: Buzzing or rattles from the door panels, seats or dash, worse in cold weather.
issues.why: Owners commonly report trim parts, seat belts and seat parts touching or vibrating.
issues.next: Note when and where the noise happens and have the dealer fix it under warranty; most fixes are padding or re-clipping.
